_meta.method_note: traxxas.com and retailer pages could not be fetched directly from this environment (network policy blocked WebFetch/curl to traxxas.com, astramodel.cz etc.). All data comes from web-search result extracts of the cited pages. Values marked confidence 'medium'/'low' should be verified against the official parts list/manual PDFs before shipping the app. UPDATE 2026-11-19: part numbers, stock gearing, battery bay and MSRP prices re-verified directly on traxxas.com (product page, exploded views, Parts Finder).
_meta.confidence_scale: high = Traxxas source plus agreement; medium = single Traxxas extract or several retailers; low = single retailer/forum or conflicting

common_breaks.fix: Replace with Traxxas 3655 heavy-duty arms; forum also suggests RPM arms for bashing (Jato-4x4 fit of specific RPM SKUs unconfirmed).
common_breaks.frequency_evidence: Single forum anecdote (arm broke on first run) plus older Jato thread recommending RPM arms

common_breaks.symptom: Bent or broken half shafts, stripped stub axles, especially on pavement
common_breaks.fix: Replace with 9051R/9052R EHD shafts or rebuild with 9058X; check hub bearing shimming.
common_breaks.frequency_evidence: RCTalk threads on Slash 4x4 VXL (shared driveline family) and used Jato reports

common_breaks.fix: Add Traxxas 9061 aluminium front shock tower brace or replace with 9033.
common_breaks.frequency_evidence: Inferred from Traxxas marketing of 9061 as 'ultimate strength upgrade'; no direct failure stats

common_breaks.fix: Spare 9032/9037/9050 EHD parts or Traxxas aluminium 9063/9064/9065.
common_breaks.frequency_evidence: Commonly upgraded part family; aftermarket aluminium sets widely sold for Jato 4x4

common_breaks.fix: Heavier rear shock oil or stiffer springs; adjust ride height.

maintenance.spec: Stock 50 wt front, 60 wt rear silicone (Traxxas 5034 / 5035)
maintenance.interval: Check for leaks after every few runs; rebuild with 7463 kit when damping fades or oil leaks (no official interval retrieved)
Not retrieved; typical practice is check/refill when diff behaviour changes

maintenance.spec: Grease from factory; can be filled with silicone diff oil
maintenance.note: Forum reports differ (some found no oil). Verify in manual.

Check wheel bearings/hub play, spin for roughness; check stub axle shimming
maintenance.interval: Regularly, especially after wet runs (waterproof electronics do not protect bearings)
